body.statement: Let \(L=3\). The deterministic selector \(S^\star\) is disconnected, equivalently every member of \(\mathcal K^*\) is disconnected, if and only if exactly one of \[d_2\geq c>b_2\qquad\text{or}\qquad1-\mu_{1,1}-\mu_{0,1}\geq c>b_3\] holds. In the first case \(k^*=2\) and \(\mathcal K^*\) is the deduplicated union of \[\bigl\{\{i-2,i\}:\mu_{1,i}+\mu_{0,0}+\mu_{0,2}-1\geq c,\ i\in X\bigr\}\] and \[\bigl\{\{-j,2-j\}:\mu_{0,j}+\mu_{1,0}+\mu_{1,2}-1\geq c,\ j\in X\bigr\}.\] In the second case \(k^*=3\) and \(\mathcal K^*=\{\{-2,0,2\}\}\). The strict and weak inequalities shown cover zero cells, exact coverage equalities, cardinality ties, span ties, and code ties.
body.justification: Ternary outcomes are the first setting with genuine holes, and the theorem supplies the complete boundary-safe phase diagram.
body.gap: ZhangRichardson2025 rules out the binary disconnected candidate, and LuDingDasgupta2018 bounds scalar ordinal events; neither gives this ternary selector partition.
body.consumer: The result provides a transparent diagnostic for three-category clinical or educational endpoints and a proof template for larger supports.
